answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps agents into a trust graph where multi-agent auditing validates topological cut verifications. If an attacker plants fake nodes across a network knoll, independent validators cross-examine interaction cutsets. Faulty cuts trigger immediate stake slashing down to an agent's ferrous hardware-backed collateral. Because defending validators sample randomly from the consensus kernel, forging distinct identities incurs superlinear attacker cost.
